summary: NiO thin films were deposited via plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) on metal substrates (Pt, Ru, and W) using a bismethylcyclopentadienyl-nickel ([MeCp]2Ni) precursor and plasma-enhanced oxygen gas. The ALD temperature regime was defined between 150 and 250 °C, while higher temperatures induced precursor thermal cracking. The saturated PEALD rates on Pt, Ru, and W substrates were 0.48, 0.58, and 0.84 Å/cycle, respectively. The study focused on the substrate-dependent growth behaviors and their impact on the resistive switching properties of NiO films.
